payload.purpose: answer_incident_question
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.

Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.

counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

Decision
Work P5 first on the integrity-review track: prioritize 600–1000 m along the pipe, around stations P5-ST4 and P5-ST5 at 700 and 900 m. Its joint pressure-loss pattern supports a suspected integrity incident, not a confirmed leak. Next, give P7 a shared-measurement-connection review at gateway-P7-0; give P2 process checks for its documented pressure-setting transition; retain P4 for a lower-priority pressure-pattern review. The accepted P5 interval is an inspection priority, not a physical leak point or dispatch approval (claim-113, claim-114).

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow confirmation for P5’s 600–1000 m focus to distinguish physical loss from an unrecorded operating or shared measurement cause.
2. Request a read-only reference-pressure comparison outside gateway-P7-0 for P7-ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, to test the shared conversion offset.
3. Request actual operating-state confirmation for P2’s recorded 90–145-second transition and P4-ST1’s pressure reduction, to determine whether those branches need further process attention.

Already checked
During elapsed seconds 130–150 of the recording, P5-ST4/ST5’s two sensors at each station measured typical deficits of 1.63–1.65 bar against normal; bar is a pressure unit. Immediately neighboring ST3/ST6 were about 1.20–1.22 bar below normal, and endpoint ST1/ST8 about 0.33–0.36 bar below normal. The final five seconds retained the central peak at about 1.65–1.68 bar below normal. Central losses persisted for 59 seconds across both shared data connections. This is stronger connected evidence than isolated alert counts.

Why this decision
P7’s odd-station readings stayed about 0.72–0.75 bar below normal throughout seconds 90–150, while even stations remained near normal. That connection-specific pattern matches the opened calibration record’s approximately −0.75 bar offset; its onset is not observed within this window. Suspect readings are P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B, not confirmed faulty hardware. P2’s broad rise of roughly 0.23–0.38 bar matches the recorded positive approximately 0.4-bar transition in sign, scale and timing. P4’s paired ST1 deficit was about 0.16 bar, with weaker downstream deficits and only two-second screening persistence. Spike flags alone do not identify unreliable P2 or P4 sensors. Full sample coverage does not establish accuracy, and health review was partial.

What changes the decision
A sustained independent P7 loss outside its shared connection, P2 changes inconsistent with or continuing beyond the recorded transition, or deterioration of P4’s joint pressure focus would change those attention tracks. P5 remains the supported first review priority while independent confirmation is sought. Incomplete operating logs and possible shared failures leave its physical cause unresolved; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1 supports comparing independent paths rather than counting agreeing taps as proof.

Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

Decision

The opened calibration record names P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B as potentially affected by a −0.75-bar conversion offset. P4-ST1-A/B have smaller typical deficits around 0.16 bar and only two-second screening persistence, not established instrument faults.

answer.text:
Decision
Work P5 first on the integrity-review track: prioritize 600–1000 m along the pipe, around stations P5-ST4 and P5-ST5 at 700 and 900 m. Its connected pressure-loss pattern supports review for a suspected leak-related integrity incident. Give P7 second attention on the instrument/connection track at gateway-P7-0, its shared data connection; give P2 process checks for the recorded pressure-setting transition; retain P4-ST1 for lower-priority pressure and operating-context review. The accepted P5 interval is an inspection priority, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval (claim-113, claim-114).

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow measurements around P5-ST4/ST5 within 600–1000 m to distinguish physical pressure loss from measurement or operating causes.
2. Request reference-pressure measurements outside gateway-P7-0 at P7-ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 to test its possible conversion offset.
3. Request actual operating-state evidence for P2’s elapsed 90–145-second transition and P4-ST1’s smaller deficit, to distinguish expected process behavior from an unexplained change.

Already checked
P5-ST4-A’s typical deficit from normal pressure was 1.655 bar; bar is a pressure unit. Nearby P5-ST3-A and P5-ST6-A deficits were 1.219 and 1.209 bar, versus 0.333 bar at P5-ST8-B. ST4-A’s final-five-second deficit remained 1.696 bar, with pressure-loss persistence over elapsed seconds 91–150. The layout places ST4 and ST5 on different data connections. These measured normal-reference deficits support the central focus; they are not changes between two readings within the recording (ev-142, ev-138, ev-150, ev-160, PROC-EXTENDED-001).

Why this decision
P7-ST1-A and P7-ST3-A remained below normal throughout elapsed seconds 90–150, with typical deficits about 0.74–0.75 bar, contrasting with near-normal P7-ST2-A. The opened calibration record names P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B as potentially affected by a −0.75-bar conversion offset. They are suspect measurement paths, not confirmed faulty sensors; an offset onset was not observed. P2-ST1-A and P2-ST8-A were typically 0.379 and 0.229 bar above normal: the direction and approximate magnitude fit its logged 0.4-bar transition. ST1-A’s rise timing matches the record; ST8-A has no reported rise period. There is no supported joint leak pattern on P2 in this window. P4-ST1-A/B have smaller typical deficits around 0.16 bar and only two-second screening persistence, not established instrument faults.

What changes the decision
Independent P7 pressure loss outside the shared connection, P2 changes beyond or inconsistent with its recorded transition, or deterioration at P4-ST1 would change those attention tracks. P5’s cause remains unresolved: operating records are incomplete and shared measurement causes still require verification. Complete sample coverage does not establish accuracy; health review was partial. KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1 supports separating a review priority from proof of physical cause.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.

Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

Decision
Work P5 first on the integrity-review track: prioritize 600–1000 m along the pipe, around stations P5-ST4 and P5-ST5 at 700 and 900 m. Its connected pressure-loss pattern supports review for a suspected leak-related integrity incident. Give P7 second attention on the instrument/connection track at gateway-P7-0, its shared data connection; give P2 process checks for the recorded pressure-setting transition; retain P4-ST1 for lower-priority pressure and operating-context review. The accepted P5 interval is an inspection priority, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval (claim-113, claim-114).

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow measurements around P5-ST4/ST5 within 600–1000 m to distinguish physical pressure loss from measurement or operating causes.
2. Request reference-pressure measurements outside gateway-P7-0 at P7-ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 to test its possible conversion offset.
3. Request actual operating-state evidence for P2’s elapsed 90–145-second transition and P4-ST1’s smaller deficit, to distinguish expected process behavior from an unexplained change.

Already checked
P5-ST4-A’s typical deficit from normal pressure was 1.655 bar; bar is a pressure unit. Nearby P5-ST3-A and P5-ST6-A deficits were 1.219 and 1.209 bar, versus 0.333 bar at P5-ST8-B. P7-ST1-A and P7-ST3-A remained below normal throughout elapsed seconds 90–150, with typical deficits about 0.74–0.75 bar, contrasting with near-normal P7-ST2-A. cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.

payload.purpose: assess_sensor_health
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.text:
Decision
Work P5 first on the integrity-review track: a suspected loss-of-containment incident, with an accepted inspection priority 600-1000 m along the pipe around P5-ST4/ST5. This is not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval. Next, review P7's shared data connection gateway-P7-0 for measurement issues. Give P2 process-context attention, P4 weaker-pressure-pattern attention plus local instrument checks, and P1/P3/P6 instrument checks rather than joint-leak labels.

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow references for P5's 600-1000 m focus and neighbouring P5-ST3/ST6, to test whether its measured deficit reflects physical pressure loss.
2. Request read-only conversion-channel status and an independent pressure reference for gateway-P7-0 at P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7, to test the recorded offset explanation.
3. Request acquisition diagnostics and independent references for the suspect instruments named below, to distinguish reading problems from hardware causes.
4. Request incident-time operating confirmation for P2's recorded 90-145 second transition and any P5 action; the opened records and available comparisons need not be repeated.

Already checked
During elapsed recording seconds 300-360, both sensors at each P5 station agree and all eight stations remain below typical baseline pressure across two data connections. Final-five-second deficits at ST4/ST5 are about 1.65-1.68 bar, versus 1.20-1.26 at neighbouring ST3/ST6 and 0.32-0.39 at ST1/ST8; bar is a pressure unit. This central peak supports the interval. Its onset was not observed; steady pressure below normal remains a deficit. P7's odd-station pairs instead show similar 0.68-0.75 bar deficits while every other station stays near baseline, matching the calibration record's magnitude and connection pattern, but not establishing onset timing.

Why this decision
The executed comparison identifies gradual upward drift at P1-ST6-A and downward drift at P3-ST7-A, with stable same-station B references; brief spikes at P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A; a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading, at P6-ST8-B; 15 invalid readings at P4-ST8-A; and 20 missing readings each at P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B. These are reading problems, not confirmed hardware failures. P5's coherent deficits do not identify unreliable sensors. P2 screening spike flags alone do not establish unreliable readings. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but individual reliability is not assured and health review is partial.

What changes the decision
The opened P2 record predicts a +0.4 bar transition during elapsed seconds 90-145; supplied measurements cover 300-360, so a sign, magnitude and timing match cannot be established. Later P2/P4 deficits are much weaker than P5's. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window for P1/P3/P6's isolated reading problems. Sustained loss outside P7's shared connection, deterioration at P5's focus, or verified operating evidence explaining P5 would change priorities. Applied KN guidance supports these distinctions, not causal certainty or operating approval.
