cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.

Your first actions

2. Request read-only conversion-channel status for gateway-P7-0 and independent pressure references at P7-ST1/ST5 and contrasting P7-ST6, to test the documented calibration explanation.
3. Request acquisition diagnostics and independent references for the eight suspect instruments listed below, to distinguish observed reading problems from hardware causes.
4. Request incident-time operating confirmation for P2's recorded transition and any P5 action; the opened records and completed comparisons need not be repeated.

Already checked
During elapsed recording seconds 300-360, P5's paired sensors—two sensors at each station—support a sustained below-normal pattern across eight stations and two data connections. Final-five-second deficits at ST4/ST5 are approximately 1.65-1.68 bar, versus 1.20-1.26 bar at neighbouring ST3/ST6; bar is a pressure unit. This central contrast supports the inspection focus under KN-LOCALIZATION-R1. The onset was not observed: steady pressure below typical baseline pressure remains a deficit, even without a new drop during the recording. On P7, reviewed A-sensor summaries at ST1/ST5 show approximately 0.75/0.68 bar deficits, while ST6-A is near baseline. That magnitude and connection contrast support checking the documented approximately -0.75 bar calibration offset, but do not establish its onset or faulty hardware.

The executed comparison identifies gradual upward drift at P1-ST6-A and downward drift at P3-ST7-A, with stable same-station B references; brief spikes at P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A; a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading, at P6-ST8-B; 15 invalid readings at P4-ST8-A; and 20 missing readings each at P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B. payload.purpose: answer_incident_question
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.text:
Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track for suspected leakage: the accepted inspection priority is 800-1200 m along the pipe, around stations ST5/ST6 at 900/1100 m. This pressure-based interval is not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval. Rank P7 next for instrument/connection checks at gateway-P7-0, its shared data connection; give P2 process attention for its recorded pressure-setting transition [claim-113, claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow observations at P6-ST5/ST6 and neighboring ST4/ST7 to test whether the pressure focus represents physical loss.
2. Request comparison of gateway-P7-0 conversion output with an independent pressure reference at P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7, and confirmation of connection assignments against the instrumentation register.
3. Request actual P2 pressure-setting feedback for elapsed seconds 90-145 and subsequent pressure/flow observations to test the documented transition. These are read-only verification requests; the review priorities can be set now.

Already checked
P6 paired sensors, meaning two sensors at each station, agree across two connection paths. During elapsed seconds 145-150 in the recording, ST5/ST6 were 1.42-1.43 bar below normal pressure; bar is a pressure unit. Neighboring ST4/ST7 were only 0.37-0.40 bar low. Central screening persistence was 59 seconds. The executed comparison found a further 0.24-0.27 bar central decline between seconds 90-110 and 110-150, with smaller neighboring changes, comparatively steady P3-ST7 and slightly rising P5-ST7. That within-record change is distinct from the larger normal-reference deficit [ev-174, ev-178, ev-182, ev-186; subsea_f3cd1f9187e44461b8ec06d06977ff92].

Why this decision
P7 odd-station readings remained 0.75-0.84 bar below normal during seconds 130-150, versus about 0.00-0.07 bar at even stations. This connection-specific pattern matches the opened calibration record's expected conversion offset, but no preceding normal period or onset step was reviewed. Target P7-ST1-A, P7-ST1-B, P7-ST3-A, P7-ST3-B, P7-ST5-A, P7-ST5-B, P7-ST7-A and P7-ST7-B; individual hardware faults are not established. P6 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable readings. P2's broad 0.38-0.42 bar rise above normal and detected 90-145 second timing match its opened record; there is no supported joint leak pattern in this window on P2, and no specific unreliable P2 sensor was identified [MAINT-P7-GW-002; OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; KN-QUALITY-R1].

What changes the decision
Deterioration of P6's focus, sustained independently confirmed loss at P7 even stations, or a new P2 change beyond the documented period would change the assessment. Complete sample coverage does not certify every instrument: health review and investigation scope remain bounded, and operating logs are incomplete. Physical causes remain unresolved; knowledge guidance supports the distinctions, not operating approval [claim-112; LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1; KN-OPERATING-R1].

Already checked
P6's paired sensors—two sensors at each station—track together across two connection paths. During elapsed seconds 145-150 in the recording, ST5/ST6 were approximately 1.42-1.43 bar below typical pressure; bar is a pressure unit. Neighboring ST4/ST7 were only approximately 0.37-0.40 bar low. Central screening persistence was 59 seconds. sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.public_output:
ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track for suspected leakage, using the accepted 800-1200 m inspection priority around stations ST5/ST6, at 900/1100 m along the pipe. This interval is not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval. Rank P7 next for measurement-connection checks at gateway-P7-0, its odd stations' shared data connection; give P2 process attention for its documented pressure-setting transition [claim-113, claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow observations at P6-ST5/ST6 and neighboring ST4/ST7 to test whether the pressure focus represents physical loss.
2. Request an independent pressure-reference comparison at P7-ST1/ST5, outside gateway-P7-0's conversion path, and confirmation of its eight-tap assignments against the instrumentation register.
3. Request actual P2 pressure-setting feedback during elapsed seconds 90-145 and afterward to explain the recorded rise and return toward typical pressure. These are read-only requests; the review priorities can be set now.

Already checked
P6's paired sensors—two sensors at each station—track together across two connection paths. The cited final-five-second measurements show ST5/ST6 approximately 1.42-1.43 bar below typical pressure; bar is a pressure unit. Neighboring ST4/ST7 were approximately 0.39 bar low. Central screening persistence was 59 seconds. The executed comparison found a further 0.24-0.27 bar central decline between seconds 90-110 and 110-150, smaller neighboring changes, comparatively steady P3-ST7 and slightly rising P5-ST7. That within-record decline is distinct from the larger normal-reference deficit [ev-174, ev-178, ev-182, ev-186; subsea_f3cd1f9187e44461b8ec06d06977ff92].

Why this decision
During elapsed seconds 130-150, P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A were respectively 0.832 and 0.739 bar below typical pressure, versus 0.064 bar at P7-ST2-A. This contrast supports checking the calibration record's expected shared conversion offset, but does not establish an onset step or eight hardware faults. Its eight-tap scope is P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B. P6 screening spike flags do not establish unreliable readings. P2's broad approximately 0.4 bar rise and detected seconds 90-145 timing match its record; cited final-five-second departures were only 0.006-0.042 bar above typical pressure, indicating substantial return. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window on P2, and no specific unreliable P2 sensor was identified [ev-194, ev-198, ev-210, ev-034, ev-052, ev-064; MAINT-P7-GW-002; OP-P2-EXTENDED-001; KN-QUALITY-R1; KN-OPERATING-R1].

What changes the decision
Deterioration of P6's focus, sustained independently confirmed pressure loss outside P7's shared connection, or a new P2 change beyond the documented period would change the assessment. Complete sample coverage does not certify local accuracy: health review and investigation scope remain bounded, and operating logs are incomplete. Physical causes remain unresolved [claim-112; LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1].
Sources: claim-113, claim-114, claim-112, ev-174, ev-178, ev-182, ev-186, ev-194, ev-198, ev-210, ev-034, ev-052, ev-064, subsea_f3cd1f9187e44461b8ec06d06977ff92, MAINT-P7-GW-002, OP-P2-EXTENDED-001, LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1
COMPETING EXPLANATIONS
leak (possible): P6 has the strongest supported joint pressure-loss pattern: paired readings agree across two connection paths, and ST5/ST6 have a substantially deeper normal-reference deficit than neighboring stations. The executed comparison shows a further central decline while P3-ST7 remains comparatively steady and P5-ST7 rises slightly, opposing a uniform network-wide loss. The numerical screening claim supports suspected-leak review and the accepted 800-1200 m inspection priority, not a confirmed physical cause or confidence percentage. Unrecorded operations or broader common measurement influences remain unexcluded; independent pressure and flow observations should test the supported focus, as localization guidance recommends.
Sources: claim-113, claim-114, ev-178, ev-182, subsea_f3cd1f9187e44461b8ec06d06977ff92, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1
instrumentation or telemetry (possible): During elapsed seconds 130-150, P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A show typical-pressure deficits of 0.832 and 0.739 bar, respectively, compared with 0.064 bar at P7-ST2-A. Their separate overall typical-pressure deficits are 0.840 and 0.770 bar; these different summaries do not establish an onset step or subsequent recovery. The opened calibration record describes an expected approximately -0.75 bar conversion offset affecting both A/B taps at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7 through gateway-P7-0. The record's eight-tap scope must not be mistaken for eight independently established faults, and the near-normal ST2-A comparison is not a suspect instrument. Independence and quality guidance support prioritizing the common measurement path while retaining concurrent physical loss as unexcluded; an independent pressure reference outside that path is the discriminating check.
Sources: ev-194, ev-198, ev-210, MAINT-P7-GW-002, KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-QUALITY-R1
operating change (possible): P2's station summaries show approximately 0.38-0.42 bar higher typical pressure than normal, and detected rise periods span elapsed seconds 90-145. The positive sign, approximate magnitude and detected timing match the opened record's expected 0.4 bar pressure-setting transition. However, the separate final-five-second baseline-relative metrics for P2-ST1-A, P2-ST5-B and P2-ST8-B are only approximately 0.006, 0.042 and 0.040 bar above typical pressure, indicating substantial return toward baseline rather than continued elevation by 0.4 bar. The record does not explain that return, and its association with P2 does not explain P6's negative focus or exclude concurrent events. Operating guidance therefore supports requesting actual pressure-setting feedback and subsequent pressure/flow observations, without assigning a sensor fault or clearing the branch.
Sources: ev-034, ev-052, ev-064, OP-P2-EXTENDED-001, LOG-EXTENDED-COVERAGE-001, KN-OPERATING-R1
Joint sensor assessment (leak pattern): P6-ST1-A, P6-ST1-B, P6-ST2-A, P6-ST2-B, P6-ST3-A, P6-ST3-B, P6-ST4-A, P6-ST4-B, P6-ST5-A, P6-ST5-B, P6-ST6-A, P6-ST6-B, P6-ST7-A, P6-ST7-B, P6-ST8-A, P6-ST8-B, P3-ST7-A, P3-ST7-B, P5-ST7-A, P5-ST7-B
The cited P6 ST5/ST6 final-five-second measurements are approximately 1.42-1.43 bar below typical pressure, versus approximately 0.39 bar at neighboring ST4/ST7. The executed synchronized comparison shows closely tracking central readings across gateway-P6-0 and gateway-P6-1, a further 0.24-0.27 bar central decrease across the split at elapsed second 110, comparatively steady P3-ST7 and slightly rising P5-ST7. Those before/after changes do not replace the larger normal-reference deficits, and the contrast supports a focused integrity-review priority rather than a uniform network-wide explanation. Localization guidance treats that pressure focus as an inspection heuristic, not a proven physical leak location; separate connection paths also do not exclude every common influence. Independent pressure/flow observations and confirmation of actual operating context and connection independence remain the useful checks.
Sources: ev-174, ev-178, ev-182, ev-186, subsea_f3cd1f9187e44461b8ec06d06977ff92, KN-LOCALIZATION-R1
QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE WITH THE ENGINEER
Do independent pressure and flow observations confirm the P6-ST5/ST6 deficit relative to neighboring ST4/ST7?
Does a pressure reference outside gateway-P7-0 disagree with P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A?
Does actual P2 pressure-setting feedback explain the transition during elapsed seconds 90-145 and the subsequent return toward typical pressure?

Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Decision
Work P6 first on the integrity-review track for suspected leakage, using the accepted 800-1200 m inspection priority around stations ST5/ST6, at 900/1100 m along the pipe. This interval is not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval. Rank P7 next for measurement-connection checks at gateway-P7-0, its odd stations' shared data connection; give P2 process attention for its documented pressure-setting transition [claim-113, claim-114; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1].

Your first actions

2. Request an independent pressure-reference comparison at P7-ST1/ST5, outside gateway-P7-0's conversion path, and confirmation of its eight-tap assignments against the instrumentation register.

Already checked
P6's paired sensors—two sensors at each station—track together across two connection paths. The cited final-five-second measurements show ST5/ST6 approximately 1.42-1.43 bar below typical pressure; bar is a pressure unit. Neighboring ST4/ST7 were approximately 0.39 bar low. Central screening persistence was 59 seconds. The executed comparison found a further 0.24-0.27 bar central decline between seconds 90-110 and 110-150, smaller neighboring changes, comparatively steady P3-ST7 and slightly rising P5-ST7. Why this decision
During elapsed seconds 130-150, P7-ST1-A and P7-ST5-A were respectively 0.832 and 0.739 bar below typical pressure, versus 0.064 bar at P7-ST2-A. payload.purpose: answer_incident_question
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.
