payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.

payload.text:
Decision
Work P6 first: prioritize integrity review for a suspected leak within the accepted 800-1200 m inspection interval, measured along the pipe around stations P6-ST5/ST6. This is a pressure-based inspection priority, not a confirmed physical leak point or dispatch approval. Next, give P7's gateway-P7-0, its shared data connection, connection-level attention. P2 needs operating-context checks plus a separate instrument check; P1/P3 need disagreeing-instrument checks, P4 needs spike/invalid-reading checks, and P5 needs a flatline check.

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow observations for P6's 800-1200 m focus, with references at stations ST4 (700 m) and ST7 (1300 m), to test whether the pressure deficit is physical.
2. Request a read-only register and calibration-output review for gateway-P7-0 and both sensors at P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7, using even-numbered stations as separate-connection references.
3. Request acquisition diagnostics and independent references for the questionable instruments below, and execution confirmation for P2's recorded pressure-setting transition at elapsed seconds 90-145. These address remaining verification boundaries, not repeat completed desk comparisons.

Already checked
During elapsed seconds 300-360 of the recording, two sensors at each P6 station ST4-ST7 agreed on sustained below-normal pressure across two data connections. ST5/ST6 were about 1.42-1.46 bar below typical pressure, versus approximately 0.38-0.41 bar at adjacent ST4/ST7; bar is a pressure unit. The completed comparison found only small within-window rises, about 0.017-0.035 bar at ST5/ST6, while P4-ST4/P5-ST4 were near normal. The deficit was already present, so its onset was not observed.

Why this decision
P7's odd-station pairs were approximately 0.75-0.86 bar below typical pressure, versus roughly 0.01-0.11 bar at even stations. This matches the calibration record's affected connection and approximate magnitude, but its onset was not observed. P2's record predicts a +0.4 bar transition at seconds 90-145; supplied later measurements cannot establish a sign, magnitude and timing match. Questionable observations are P1-ST6-A/P3-ST7-A: sustained paired disagreement with suspected drift; P2-ST3-A/P3-ST7-B/P4-ST7-B: brief spike flags; P1-ST7-B/P3-ST5-B: missing readings; P4-ST8-A: invalid readings; P5-ST8-B: a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading. These do not confirm hardware faults. Coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial; P6 screening spike counts do not establish unreliable sensors.

What changes the decision
Independent deterioration at P6 strengthens integrity concern. Sustained independent loss outside P7's shared connection, or pressure departures beyond P2's recorded transition, would change those branches' attention tracks. Incomplete operating logs leave competing causes unresolved. KN-QUALITY-R1 and KN-LOCALIZATION-R1 support separating observation problems from physical pressure evidence and an inspection interval from leak coordinates.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.

Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.

answer.text:
Decision
Work P6 first: give integrity review priority to a suspected leak pattern around stations P6-ST5/ST6, within the accepted 800-1200 m inspection interval measured along the pipe. This interval is an inspection priority, not a confirmed leak point or dispatch approval. Next, prioritize P7's gateway-P7-0 shared data connection for measurement-path checks. P2 needs operating-transition confirmation and a separate instrument check; P1/P3 need disagreeing-instrument checks, P4 needs spike and invalid-reading checks, and P5 needs a flatline check.

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure and flow observations around P6's 800-1200 m focus, with pressure references at ST4 (700 m) and ST7 (1300 m), to distinguish physical pressure loss from measurement bias.
2. Request a read-only instrumentation-register and calibration-output review for gateway-P7-0 and both A/B sensors at P7-ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7, with even-numbered stations as separate-connection references. This tests the recorded shared conversion-path explanation.
3. Request acquisition diagnostics and independent references for the affected instruments below, plus execution confirmation and transition-period measurements for P2's recorded change at elapsed seconds 90-145. These address remaining evidence gaps rather than repeat completed comparisons.

Already checked
During elapsed seconds 300-360 of the recording, P6-ST4 through ST7 had sustained below-normal pressure with agreeing paired sensors, meaning two sensors at each station, across two data connections. At elapsed seconds 340-360, P6-ST5-A was approximately 1.43 bar below typical pressure, versus 0.38 bar at neighboring P6-ST4-A and 0.40 bar at P6-ST7-B; bar is a pressure unit. The central deficit was therefore roughly one bar greater than at those neighbors. The completed comparison found only small rises, approximately 0.017-0.035 bar at ST5/ST6, within the later window. Those rises do not erase the existing deficit; its onset was not observed.

Why this decision
P7-ST1-A was approximately 0.85 bar below typical pressure, broadly consistent with the calibration record's possible -0.75 bar bias. That record names the other odd-station pairs, but does not prove faulty sensors or establish an observed calibration onset. P2's record predicts a +0.4 bar transition at elapsed seconds 90-145; the supplied later measurements cannot establish a sign, magnitude and timing match. Questionable observations are P1-ST6-A/P3-ST7-A: sustained paired disagreement and suspected drift; P2-ST3-A/P3-ST7-B/P4-ST7-B: brief spike flags; P1-ST7-B/P3-ST5-B: missing readings; P4-ST8-A: invalid readings; P5-ST8-B: a flatline, meaning an unchanging reading. These are observation problems, not confirmed hardware faults. Health review is partial, and P6 screening spike counts alone do not establish unreliable sensors.

What changes the decision
Independent deterioration at P6 strengthens integrity concern. Sustained independent pressure loss outside P7's shared connection, or departures outside P2's recorded transition period, would change those branches' attention tracks. KN-QUALITY-R1 supports separating questionable observations from physical pressure evidence; independent confirmation remains the physical verification boundary, not a reason to defer P6's supported review priority.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.

Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.

Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, rather than selecting a pipeline leak-inspection section. Next, give instrument attention to P3-ST7-A at 1,300 m along P3 and P1-ST6-A at 1,100 m along P1, plus the P4/P6 reading problems below. Give P2 process attention: its broad pressure rise matches the opened operating record. P5's reviewed pressure summaries show no sustained negative region. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window and no qualified inspection interval: independent negative-pressure corroboration is inadequate. P3-ST7 is a station-level verification focus, not a leak location.

Your first actions
1. Request an independent pressure reference for P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 and read-only confirmation of gateway-P7-0's conversion configuration and calibration-test status; distinguish actual pressure loss from the shared reading offset.
2. Request independent references at P3-ST7 and P1-ST6, alongside their stable B sensors; resolve the single-sensor downward and upward drifts without treating either as a joint pipeline event.
3. Request read-only instrument diagnostics for P4-ST7-B, P6-ST3-A and P6-ST8-B, and data-delivery status for P1-ST7-B, P3-ST5-B and P4-ST8-A; distinguish spikes, a stuck reading and observation gaps.

Already checked
The specialists compared P7's two sensors at each station before and after 90 seconds elapsed in the recording. The eight odd-station readings stepped down by 0.704-0.739 bar, a pressure unit, and remained shifted. Their recent typical pressures are 0.724-0.742 bar below normal; even-station pressures are approximately 0.007-0.037 bar above normal. This is a persistent offset, not a flatline. Its timing and magnitude match the revised calibration record's approximately -0.75 bar effect. All eight share one connection, so agreement is not independent confirmation.

Why this decision
P3-ST7-A gradually falls while its paired B reference stays stable: recent typical pressure is 0.505 bar below normal, increasing to a 0.690 bar deficit in the final five seconds. P1-ST6-A drifts upward, reaching 0.713 bar above normal in the final five seconds; its B reference remains near normal. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief spikes; P6-ST8-B is flat throughout the latest 60-second record. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 samples; P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid readings excluded. These are questionable observations, not confirmed hardware faults. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial. P2's approximately 0.40-0.43 bar rise above normal and recorded 90-145-second rise period match its documented positive 0.4 bar pressure-setting transition.

What changes the decision
A sustained loss confirmed outside P7's shared connection, independent agreement at P3-ST7, or a P2 change inconsistent with the recorded operating period would change the attention track. The available comparisons are already complete; independent physical pressure and flow confirmation remains the boundary for establishing a cause. The operating excerpt is incomplete, and advisory KN guidance does not establish a fault or authorize intervention.

Decision
Review P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, first: it serves both A/B sensors at ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, located 100, 500, 900 and 1,300 m along P7. The strongest supported priority is a measurement-connection check, not pipeline leak inspection. Next, prioritize instrument checks at P3-ST7 and P1-ST6, then the P4/P6 observation problems below. P2 needs process-context attention because its pressure rise matches the opened operating record. There is no supported joint leak pattern in this window. A qualified inspection interval is withheld because independent negative-pressure corroboration is inadequate; P3-ST7 is a station-level verification focus, not a leak location.

Your first actions
1. Request independent pressure references at P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 and read-only confirmation of gateway-P7-0's conversion configuration and calibration-test status. This distinguishes physical pressure loss from a shared reading offset.
2. Request independent pressure references at P3-ST7, 1,300 m along P3, and P1-ST6, 1,100 m along P1. Compare them with the existing A/B readings to resolve the disagreement between two sensors at each station.
3. Request read-only diagnostics for P4-ST7-B, P6-ST3-A and P6-ST8-B, plus data-delivery and validity diagnostics for P1-ST7-B, P3-ST5-B and P4-ST8-A. These checks distinguish brief spikes, a stuck reading and observation gaps.

Already checked
The P7 comparison shows eight odd-station readings stepping down by 0.704-0.739 bar, a pressure unit, around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording and remaining shifted. Every other station has small positive before/after changes. Separately, P7-ST1-A's recent typical pressure is 0.724 bar below normal, while P7-ST2-A is 0.037 bar above normal. A stable post-step profile does not erase that deficit. The revised calibration record describes the same timing and approximately -0.75 bar offset. Under KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, agreement through one shared connection is not independent leak confirmation.

Why this decision
P3-ST7-A drifts downward, reaching 0.763 bar below normal in the final five seconds; P1-ST6-A drifts upward, reaching 0.891 bar above normal. Their B partners remain stable. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each show two brief spikes; P6-ST8-B is flat in the latest 60-second summary. P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B each miss 20 of 60 samples; P4-ST8-A has 15 excluded invalid readings. These are questionable observations, not confirmed hardware faults. Overall usable coverage is 99.18%, but health review is partial. P2-ST1-A's recent typical pressure is 0.404 bar above normal, with a recorded rise period of 90-145 seconds, matching the logged positive 0.4 bar pressure-setting transition in sign, magnitude and timing. KN-OPERATING-R1 supports a different attention track for that branch.

What changes the decision
Sustained independent pressure loss outside P7's shared connection, independent agreement with P3-ST7-A's decline, or a P2 change inconsistent with the recorded operating period would change the priority. The reviewed comparisons and records already support this desk-review decision; independent physical pressure and flow confirmation remains necessary to establish a cause. Operating-log coverage is incomplete, and unreviewed instruments cannot be declared reliable.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.

counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.

verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. Decision
Work first on P7's shared data connection, gateway-P7-0, serving both A/B sensors at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7, at 100, 500, 900 and 1300 metres along P7. This is an instrument/connection review priority, not a pipeline leak inspection interval. Next, give P1-ST6-A and P3-ST7-A instrument checks; keep P2 on the process-check track and P4/P6 on targeted reading-quality checks. P5 has no supported joint leak pattern in the reviewed measurements. No qualified pipeline section can be recommended for inspection: the accepted evidence lacks sufficient independent observers for localization.

Your first actions
1. Request an independent pressure reference at P7 ST3 and adjacent ST2/ST4, outside gateway-P7-0, to distinguish a real pressure loss from a shared conversion offset.
2. Request independent reference readings at P1 ST6 and P3 ST7 alongside their A/B taps, to resolve the single-sensor disagreement.
3. Request read-only acquisition-status evidence for P6-ST8-B, P4-ST8-A, P1-ST7-B and P3-ST5-B to distinguish stuck, invalid and missing readings from process changes.

Already checked
The opened P7 calibration record predicts an approximately 0.75 bar downward offset; bar is a pressure unit. The executed comparison shows all eight affected taps stepping down by 0.704-0.739 bar around 90 seconds into the recording, while even-numbered stations change only +0.005 to +0.035 bar. Current summaries still show deficits of roughly 0.73-0.76 bar from typical pressure, whereas ST2 is within about 0.01 bar of its reference. These are baseline-relative deficits, not evidence of a new drop late in the recording. The P2 ST3 pair rose about 0.41 bar during the logged 90-145-second pressure-setting transition and returned close to its earlier level afterward, matching the record's sign, magnitude and timing.

Why this decision
P1-ST6-A is drift-suspect and about 3.63 bar above typical pressure in the final five seconds; P3-ST7-A is drift-suspect and about 3.61 bar below typical pressure. Their paired B sensors remain close to their references. P4-ST7-B and P6-ST3-A each have two brief spike flags; P4-ST8-A has 15 invalid readings, and P1-ST7-B/P3-ST5-B each lack 20 of 60 readings. P6-ST8-B is an observed flatline, with zero pressure variation. These patterns justify checks, not confirmed hardware faults. Aggregate coverage of 99.18% does not establish local reliability, and health review is partial.

What changes the decision
Following KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, agreement through one shared connection is not independent leak evidence. Sustained pressure loss outside gateway-P7-0, worsening independent station readings, or a P2 change beyond its recorded transition would increase integrity-review priority. Physical pressure/flow confirmation remains necessary; the present evidence neither confirms a leak nor clears the pipelines.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the numerical tool's actual method and retain its assumptions. The default method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours. On extended networks, a broad continuous pressure footprint may leave no unaffected neighbours or an overly wide bracket. The pressure-peak-focus fallback can then identify a priority inspection focus from the final five seconds of fully observed paired readings: a unique contiguous pressure-deficit peak, agreeing pairs, independent comparison paths and weaker immediately neighbouring stations whose contrast exceeds the baseline-noise allowance. Missing comparisons, tied/disconnected peaks, inadequate independence and excessive width still withhold a focus. Those comparison stations need not be unaffected. This is a spatial pressure-focus heuristic, not a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem or a guarantee that a physical leak lies inside the interval. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact leak coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or a research formula without its inputs. Physical intervention still requires the approved site procedure and operator authorization.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check eligibility, paired coverage, observer independence, actual method and bounding comparisons.
State the priority interval and explain whether its neighbours are unaffected or simply weaker; do not call it a confidence interval or confirmed leak point.
Keep physical confirmation and operator authorization separate from the completed pressure-pattern assessment; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.
